title: Device semantics stay above USB presentation mechanics
summary: VirtualUsbDevice and Fido2Authenticator own semantic device/FIDO behavior. LinuxRawGadgetProvider owns Raw Gadget ioctls, endpoint handles and blocking transfer mechanics. FidoTestHost is a synthetic in-process memory-provider host and must not be used as the Linux Raw Gadget host.
invariants: Fido2Authenticator does not call Raw Gadget, ioctl, hidraw or kernel USB APIs.
CTAP2 semantics remain above CTAPHID framing, which remains above VirtualUsbEndpoint.
LinuxRawGadgetProvider is a presentation adapter, not the FIDO application.
FidoTestHost depends on the memory provider's synthetic writes/hostOut contract and is not a real-host bridge.
Do not add fake memory-provider messages such as writes to LinuxRawGadgetProvider merely to satisfy FidoTestHost.
procedure: Test semantic FIDO behavior through the memory provider.
Test physical Linux-host behavior through the real Raw Gadget presenter with Linux as host.
Change the smallest owning layer when a failure is localized.

provenance.claim: Architecture records the provider-neutral device/FIDO layering and Raw Gadget concurrency boundary.
FidoTestHost is the synthetic test-host harness used with memory-provider behavior.
